plans.authentic_start: Normal engine-reassembly stage: crankshaft/lower crankcase already assembled and rear seal not installed; genuine new seal and actual SST/hammer loose at reachable work surface. Earlier teardown and later head/oil-pan/engine mounting outside bounded scope, explicitly disclosed. Preserve full relevant block, shaft and flange; do not replace with a generic open ring trainer or start seal correctly pre-aligned/partly pressed.
plans.authentic_endpoint: Seal case seated square to real block rear-face datum with lip around actual crankshaft; no visible folded lip/ejected garter spring/case distortion. Claim mechanical installation only, not certified oil tightness or completed engine service.

known_source_numeric.seal_face_axial_offset: Nominal flush =0mm relative to block rear face, source qualitative aligned/flush. No source allowable ±band supplied.

numeric_TBD: Tap impulse/energy/force versus insertion depth and cock angle
Allowed flush/tilt band and gauge repeatability for simple physical score
Permitted lip stretch/shaft contact friction and lip/spring material parameters

observations: Measure case recess/projection relative to block rear face at several circumferential points with simple depth/straightedge method; source endpoint is flush, not a count of taps.

Observe orientation and lip/garter spring condition by available assembly-side views or ordinary inspection mirror if accessible in this genuine rebuild state; validate visibility rather than cutting a viewing slot into the block.
Real negative controls: partly cocked seal, reversed seal, folded/rolled lip or displaced spring, correct-looking outer face with wrong actual interface.
Hands and tools released from completed seal; retain correct installed position. Failure/damage cannot earn full credit.
physical_score_design.limits: No implemented scorer or numerical tolerance is claimed. Need a short real-specimen measurement rehearsal. A simple inspection failure is a scoring-design question, not automatic rejection; accepted #1562/#1576 show mechanical assembly need not simulate full fluid certification. Do not claim leak proof from pose.

plans.permitted_research_model: Mostly rigid driver, hammer, real case and block/shaft contacts; bounded compliant sealing lip and calibrated axial interference/friction are proportionate candidates. Must retain unstarted alignment, real driver engagement, cocking/jam/damage counterexamples and actual released seat. Do not script final seal pose, weld on depth threshold or infer successful lip seating from hammer action count. No simulation implementation was made.
YAM_access_force_obstacles: 93.9mm nominal aperture is not an OD guarantee; actual seal OD unknown. Determine whether ordinary rim/edge grasp remains accessible without enlargement.
Driver around real crankshaft/flange must leave stock finger/palm clearance at all positions; fingertips/TCP alone insufficient.
One hand holding real driver and the other controlling hammer introduces contact/impact/reaction beyond a static press. Source permits tapping, not an invented push-button press.
7Nm wrist configuration/50N gripper setting do not certify impact energy, grasp slip or reachable loaded posture.

exact_proposed_components.value: One valve station in a full 2013 Elantra L4-1.8L cylinder head, genuine valve/stem groove and installed stem seal.
exact_proposed_components.evidence: p230/231 and exploded view p229 image673971832.jpeg; do not substitute generic preload fixture.
Actual p4300 parts table; current VIN/supersession remains to confirm.

exact_proposed_components.value: HYD2222302500 (22223-02500), two actual mating halves for one valve.
exact_proposed_components.evidence: Actual p4302 part table; p229 exploded drawing viewed shows paired lock pieces. No assumed generic pins.

p230/231 specify this matched tool. Image676307272.jpeg viewed: real full-head mounted support/lever, front support inserted directly into head bolt hole as text states. Do not assume OTC interchangeability or invent a preload actuator.

plans.authentic_start: Full actual head normally supported for valve reassembly, with a genuine valve/stem already inserted and stem seal installed as the preceding documented operation. Spring, retainer and two locks are not already captured; include spring/retainer placement or disclose a legitimate staged start that retains the actual compression/keeper engagement. Source requires spring enamel-marked side toward retainer. Actual head support and SST mounting need to be specified; no enlarged opening or printed generic head.
plans.authentic_endpoint: Both actual keeper halves seated in valve-stem groove/retainer taper, spring load transferred from genuine compressor to the real captured assembly, retained after the source-supported push/release check and final tool disengagement. Not a hidden installed flag or friction-only custom fork.

known_source_numeric.check_cycles_source: Push/release compressor handle2–3times before final release; a proposed3-cycle check lies within that source range. It is a legitimate equipment verification, not an invented repeated event.

numeric_TBD: Correct reference datum for12mm retainer travel at chosen legitimate start
Actual spring rate, installed length, preload and force curve
Tool pivot/retainer-contact/handle lever arms, handle span, mass and friction
Actual keeper OD/height/taper/groove dimensions and available insertion gap
Real normal support stability/reaction, stock gripper/tool access and torque/slip
Meaningful measurement tolerance for keeper seating and retained valve/retainer motion
plans.force_analysis: Free height45.93mm and a12mm travel limit do NOT determine spring force or stored energy. For a simple lever, F_handle≈F_spring*r_contact/r_handle plus friction; r values and spring force must be measured on this actual SST/application. The head/tool support carries reaction as the real assembly does; no task actuator may secretly hold or compress the spring. 7Nm wrist and50N jaw-effort constants are different quantities and cannot be compared directly to spring force. If a correctly mounted lever reduces effort, that is authentic mechanism advantage, not a shortcut.

observations: Two distinct keeper halves engage actual stem groove and retainer taper; correct visual split/height after tool release.
Retainer stays captured under genuine spring load after actual2–3handle check cycles. No missing/tilted half, incorrect groove, folded contact or overtravel.
Observe real retainer travel with ruler/marker/video or other simple gauge in the genuine fixture; calibrate source travel datum rather than arbitrary simulator zero.
One-half/tilted-half/incorrect-taper negative controls must fail final released capture; full credit cannot come from a held compressed spring.
physical_score_design.partial_credit: Pre-release genuinely placed parts can support partial progress; do not reward a damaged unsafe released assembly. Final outcome is load-bearing capture rather than arbitrary process order.
physical_score_design.limits: No completed physical scoring rehearsal or numeric keeper-seat tolerance. No injury/safety category inferred merely from stored energy. No claim to have built or certified an engine.

plans.permitted_research_model: Rigid real head, valve/stem, tapered keepers, retainer and articulated real SST lever with calibrated axial spring law. Bounded compliance/friction or a disclosed contact approximation can be proportionate if actual load transfer, slip/ejection and one-half failure remain. No distance-triggered latch/weld, prescribed keeper motion, spring weaker than actual selected part, or generic key-slot puzzle. Reading simulator state for future expert planning is allowed; robot actions must cause movement.
YAM_access_force_obstacles: Full genuine head/SST handle sweep and real tool mounting through head hole; no miniature head.
Stem is about5.47mm across, so stock fingers may obstruct keeper access even when the local aperture admits the part; tiny locks and deep spring cup need genuine actual dimensions.

While one arm controls lever, the other must place both halves without the first being held by a scripted magnet or adhesive. If an ordinary genuine pickup tool/forceps is needed, source/real use must be bound; the current procedure does not specify such a tool.
Need actual legitimate stability of one half while retrieving/placing the other; unsupported extra hand or invented fixture is an early kill.
Part numbers/source instructions do not establish attainable robot force or repeatable grip.

cheap_kill_gates.test: Bind genuine parts222212E000/2222302500/222222E000 and SST to selected full head; map keeper-opening dimensions and lever support from actual drawings/sample.
cheap_kill_gates.no_go: Only enlarged keepers, generic loaded cage, invented seating shoulders or weakened spring make access possible.

cheap_kill_gates.test: Stock-gripper/palm and actual permitted pickup-tool1:1 overlay through source-supported compression range; confirm both halves can be sequentially placed and remain legitimate before release.
cheap_kill_gates.no_go: Necessary grip blocks spring cup/stem, first half only stays with hidden attachment, or a third robot hand is required without a real normal assembly aid.

cheap_kill_gates.test: Measure actual SST handle force versus retainer displacement and support stability using the selected spring; respect12mm limit.
cheap_kill_gates.no_go: Force/torque/sweep cannot fit a legitimate YAM pose and reaction path; do not infer feasibility from lever picture or travel alone.

cheap_kill_gates.test: Available real sample: compare full pair, absent half and tilted half through gradual load release and source2–3check cycles. Record photos/displacement and failures.
cheap_kill_gates.no_go: Real retained condition cannot be scored simply, or a model would need disconnected capture flags to pass the counterexamples.

plans.relative_cost: Higher thanN044: actual SST assembly is useful bounded mechanics, but tiny two-half manipulation, first-half stability, spring force/reaction and released positive capture couple tightly. Keep visible as credible source-backed backup, not a default expensive build.

execution: Source/geometry/analytical research only; no hardware, task implementation, GPU/native, paid work or official submission.
